verdictStatement: Two of the three claimed repairs are genuine and verified: claude2v4 now records my three v4 advisories with a matching unfolded declaration, and claude2v1HistoricalPin is restored with a digest I checked against the live file, which also un-dangles the ADV-4 entry. The contract itself is untouched — seventeen substantive keys byte-identical to v5 — and no other attack lands, including after HEAD moved to 9af5060 mid-review, which broke no pin. The third repair fails, and fails in the direction that costs the most. My v5 S-3 offered two fixes for the CLAUDE-V3-ADV-2 accounting: swap the two halves, or delete reviewGuidance index 19 and declare it fully folded. v6 performed neither. It left the array untouched — reviewGuidance is not on its roster and is byte-identical to v5, with 'Do not mark DR-101 SATISFIED.' still at indices 12 and 19 — and rewrote the sentence to say the duplicate 'was removed at v4' and that ADV-2 'is fully folded', then deleted the item from notFoldedThisSuccessor. The document's own roster proves it never touched the array it claims to have cleaned, and the item that was at least visible as outstanding at v5 now has no trace anywhere. Separately, claude2v5 omits the advisories field, erasing my two v5 advisories from the ledger with no declaration — the same defect this successor exists to repair, corrected for the v4 record and recreated in the v5 record added by the same edit. I confirmed the Codex twin is harmless because that verdict truly carried none, which isolates the loss to the Claude record for the third version running.

coordinatorNote: REJECT of the artifact, not a disposition of the row. DR-101 stays OPEN at file 08 line 283. The design contract has now been clean and unchanged for three consecutive versions; every finding at v4, v5 and v6 has been in the honesty ledger, and both findings here are text edits in /appliesFindingsOf and /honestyRepairsFromV3. Deleting one line from reviewGuidance would make S-1's claim true outright. I want to be direct about the pattern rather than just log a fourth round. The ADV-2 duplicate has now been misrecorded across four successive versions, escalating each time — introduced at v4, called removed at v5, called fully folded and struck from the outstanding list at v6 — and Claude-lane advisories have been dropped from the ledger at v5 and again at v6, each time in the record added by the very edit repairing the previous instance. The per-round review loop is correcting named instances without correcting the practice, and it is now consuming more effort than the contract did. My recommendation is that the coordinator stop dispatching per-finding successors and instead specify the ledger's required shape once — a fixed schema for each verdict record with a mandatory advisories array, and a rule that no fold may be asserted for a path the roster does not include — then have one successor rebuild the ledger against it. That single constraint would have prevented every finding I have raised since v4. Finally, two scope notes: HEAD advanced to 9af5060 (D-108) during this review and I re-verified every pin afterwards with no effect on grading, and I read the Codex v5 verdict because the dispatch barred only the current reviewer, which is what let me confirm its record is accurate.
